title: Convert Sorted List to Binary Search Tree
statement:
`head` is the first node of a singly linked list whose values are sorted in non-decreasing order (it may be `null` for an empty list). Build a binary search tree out of all the list's values and return its root. The tree must satisfy both rules:

- **Search order:** an in-order traversal (left subtree, then the node, then the right subtree) visits the values exactly as they appear in the list.
- **Height balance:** at every node, the heights of the left and right subtrees differ by at most one.

More than one tree can satisfy these rules; any of them is accepted. An empty list produces an empty tree (`null`).
constraints: The list has between 0 and 2 * 10^4 nodes
The values are sorted in non-decreasing order
notes:
## Intuition

The middle value of a sorted list makes a natural root: everything before it belongs in the left subtree and everything after it in the right. Splitting at the middle again and again keeps the two sides within one node of each other, which keeps the tree height-balanced. The simplest version copies the list into an array so the middle is one index away; here the middle is found inside the list itself with slow and fast pointers.

## Approach

1. Define `build(start, end)`, which builds a tree from the nodes from `start` up to, but not including, `end`.
2. If `start === end` the range is empty, so return `null`.
3. Move `slow` one step and `fast` two steps at a time until `fast` reaches `end` or would step onto it. `slow` is then the middle node.
4. Make `root` from `slow.val`, build its left subtree from `[start, slow)` and its right subtree from `[slow.next, end)`.
5. The answer is `build(head, null)`.

## Example 1, step by step

The list is `-10 → -3 → 0 → 5 → 9`. In `build(-10, null)`, `fast` visits `-10`, `0`, `9` while `slow` visits `-10`, `-3`, `0`, so the root is `0`. The left range `[-10, -3]` has `slow` stop at `-3`, which gets `-10` as its left child. The right range `[5, 9]` has `slow` stop at `9`, which gets `5` as its left child. The tree is `[0,-3,9,-10,null,5]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n log n): each recursion level scans every node at most once in total, and there are about log n levels.
- Space: O(log n) for the recursion, plus the n tree nodes that make up the answer.

## Pitfalls

- The loop needs both checks, `fast !== end` and `fast.next !== end`; otherwise `fast` runs past the range into the next part of the list.
- Bounding each range by `end` leaves the list intact. Cutting the list instead needs the node before the middle; if the cut is missed, the left call sees the whole list again and never stops recursing.
- The right range starts at `slow.next`, not `slow`, or the middle value appears twice.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `build` | builds a balanced tree from the range `[start, end)` |
| `start`, `end` | first node of the range and the node just after it |
| `slow` | moves one step at a time; ends on the middle node |
| `fast` | moves two steps at a time; tells `slow` when to stop |
| `root` | the tree node made from the middle value |
